paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We show the empirical generalization errors (termed Error in the figures) and estimated Hessian traces of the loss for fine-tuned adapters (using QAdapter on Llama-3-8B) across various hidden dimensions. Smaller adapters achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima.

model_annotations.English: This line plot, titled "Errors (BoolQ)," illustrates the relationship between rank values and their corresponding errors. The x-axis is labeled "Rank" and employs a logarithmic scale with discrete tick marks placed at values of 4, 16, 64, and 256, without specific units. The y-axis lacks an explicit label but utilizes a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 0.6, with tick marks spaced at regular numeric intervals of 0.2. The plot features a single solid black line with large green circular markers and vertical black error bars at each data point. The line begins at an x-axis value of 4 with a y-axis value of approximately 0.27. It exhibits a slight decline to its lowest point of approximately 0.24 at an x-axis value of 16. Following this initial drop, the line demonstrates a steady upward trend, rising to a value of roughly 0.30 at an x-axis value of 64, and concluding at a peak y-axis value of approximately 0.35 at the final x-axis value of 256.
